clue.text: Impatient travellers who don't wait to see 11

definitions.text: Impatient travellers who don't wait to see 11

parts.words: Impatient travellers who don't wait to see 11
parts.note: 11 is the first word of 11/16, a colour on traffic lights; drivers who race through on the warning light are betting they will get across before it changes

explanation.surface: A complaint about restless travellers who never wait for something to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 refers to 11-across, the light that follows the warning one. Drivers who push on through the warning light gamble rather than wait for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical coinage for motorists who take a chance on the traffic signal before it turns to stop.

clue.text: Letter said nothing more to resolve — one's 9

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter A is spoken as Alfa

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it down and sort it out, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone spells out a letter, says nothing further, and leaves the matter to be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resolve' rearranges O and MORE into ROMEO, itself another NATO letter. 'one's 9' plays on 9-across: a car is something that is driven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian sports car is a vehicle that gets driven, so it is one that is 'driven'.

clue.text: Elite force maintained attack on all sides

indicators.note: maintained means held or kept, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: the elite are the best
the setter uses E, the physics symbol for energy, loosely for force

explanation.surface: A crack military unit keeps up its assault from every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintained' puts E inside BEST. Using E for force is loose, since E normally stands for energy, but the setter clearly intends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surrounded and harassed on every front, as by enemies or troubles.

clue.text: About ten thousand invested in transatlantic runner

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into a venture

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ten is written as the figures 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Sounds like a financial story about ten thousand being put into an Atlantic-crossing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a crossword term for a river, and from Britain a river in North America is across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river forming part of the US-Mexico border flows on the far side of the ocean from Britain.

clue.text: Rogers partner — mostly it's a real struggle

indicators.note: to struggle is to twist and writhe, so the letters are thrown into a new order
mostly means all but the last bit, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that being Rogers's partner is mostly a real struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the L from ITSAREAL, leaving ITSAREA, and 'struggle' rearranges those letters. 'Rogers' looks like any surname; it is Ginger Rogers, the dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred, the Hollywood dancer, partnered Ginger Rogers in a string of 1930s musical films.

clue.text: Funds short so move

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a budget is the money set aside for something

explanation.surface: Money is tight, so someone has to relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something even slightly is to make it give way or stir from its place.

clue.text: English terrain's suited to countrymen

indicators.note: suited here means made to fit, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Some English landscape is said to suit people from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' rearranges E with TERRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Horn of Africa state are compatriots, fellow nationals of that land.

clue.text: Went with Santander's original rate

indicators.note: original means the first, so the opening letter of the bank's name is taken

parts.note: went is a coy euphemism for urinated, as in 'went to the loo'

explanation.surface: Someone banked with Santander at its original interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like a plain verb of motion; it is the euphemism, giving PEED, with S from Santander placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is the rate at which something moves, as in 'at a rate of knots'.

clue.text: Bad fire at development

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: A bad blaze breaks out at a housing development.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-off or branch that grows out of something larger is a development from it.

clue.text: Did investor go wrong with purchase? Very annoyed

indicators.note: go wrong means come out badly, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: purchase can mean a firm grip, as does traction

explanation.surface: Did a shareholder blunder on an acquisition? Then someone is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wrong' rearranges DIDINVESTOR into DRIVENTODIS, which is then followed by TRACTION. 'purchase' looks like buying; it means grip.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being pushed to the edge of exasperation, so vexed one can no longer think straight.

clue.text: Get friendly with fellow's bird grabbing rear? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so one piece goes into another
this swaps the roles, so the word for rear does the grabbing and the bird goes inside

parts.note: to rear is to bring up, or raise
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A man's bird pinches his backside, an over-familiar gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' swaps the roles of 'grabbing', so the word for rear holds the bird. 'rear' looks like a backside; it is the verb to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix socially and amicably with others, especially those on the opposing side.

clue.text: Flower that's on racecourse land

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire with a well-known horse racing track
a land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A bloom grows somewhere on the ground of a racing track.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a racecourse in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson variety of the clove pink, a garden bloom often worn as a buttonhole.

clue.text: I think there's information on Shakespearean heroine

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the second piece comes next

parts.note: IMO is the texting abbreviation for 'in my opinion'
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone believes there are facts available about a heroine of the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: The virtuous princess of Cymbeline is a leading lady from the playwright's work.

clue.text: Good on exotic dancer getting resident's permit

parts.note: re can mean on, as in on the subject of

indicators.note: exotic means strange or unusual, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer is gratefully granted residency papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the crossword convention RE, meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: The US document allowing a foreign national to live and work there permanently.

clue.text: Cheap yet fashionable pirate accessory?

indicators.note: fashionable is read as able to be fashioned, so the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: An item that's inexpensive but trendy for a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges CHEAPYET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover worn over one eye is the stock costume item of a buccaneer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Turning against drugs gets very good as a crusader

indicators.note: turning means facing about, so the short pieces are read backwards

parts.note: V for versus means against
E is slang for ecstasy, used for drugs
angelic means extremely well-behaved

explanation.surface: Someone who turns against drugs becomes saintly, like a campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reads V and E backwards as EV.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealously promoting a cause, in the manner of a campaigner for it.

clue.text: See 11
Predecessor backing Echo's stand

parts.note: to be for something is to back it
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to stand something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A forerunner supports a nymph's position.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is someone who came before, one of those who went earlier.

clue.text: Say, chicken in car finally thawed out

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is taken away from the car

parts.note: a roadster is an open two-seater car

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A frozen bird left in a vehicle has at last defrosted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes D, the last letter of 'thawed', and 'out' removes it from ROADSTER. 'Say' marks the definition as an example: a chicken is one bird reared for roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of a size suited to cooking in the oven; a chicken is a typical example.

clue.text: Coming back over, US sailor keeps promise

indicators.note: Coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
keeps means holds within, so the letters are held inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An American seaman returns and stays true to his word.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'keeps promise' as the definition, but 'keeps' is the hidden-word signal holding ERUSSA, reversed by 'Coming back'; ASSURE means promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your word that something is so is to pledge or guarantee it.

clue.text: Lover offers nothing new

parts.note: sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A suitor has no novelty to bring.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is a British slang phrase meaning nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast or devotee, someone who loves a team or a performer.

clue.text: Take in duke initially

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, from rhyming slang Duke of Yorks for forks
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A nobleman is brought in at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duke' looks like a nobleman; it is slang for a fist, as in 'put up your dukes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin with, at the outset, before anything else happens.

clue.text: Drop into 20D, perhaps causing rage

parts.note: read as an instruction, the solution says alter the letters of a word for kit, which produces the clue's word for fury

explanation.surface: Slipping into first, perhaps, makes someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the solution read as wordplay rearranges GEAR to make RAGE. 20D is FIRST, the lowest gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting down to the lowest ratio on a car's gearbox is an example of selecting a different cog.

clue.text: Calls to pick up spectacles

indicators.note: to pick up means to hear, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: spectacles are impressive sights

explanation.surface: Someone telephones to collect their glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' looks like glasses; it means sights, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone to appear in court, or to name a source as an authority.

clue.text: Architect's grand — A1 possibly

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
the A1 is a small model made by the German carmaker, so the maker is suggested by an example

explanation.surface: An architect's work is grand, possibly first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A1' looks like a mark of excellence; it is a car model.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoni, the Catalan designer of the Sagrada Familia in Barcelona.

clue.text: Absolute guarantee — wife won't be there

indicators.note: won't be there means is absent, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a warranty or guarantee can be called a warrant

explanation.surface: Total assurance given that a spouse will be absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter, out-and-out, as in 'arrant nonsense'.

clue.text: One-off letter that's inclined to include vilification of law book

indicators.note: include means take inside, so one piece goes within the other
off here means taken away, so the one is removed from the slanting letter

parts.note: italic type slopes to the right
one is the Roman numeral I
mud is slander, as in mudslinging

explanation.surface: A unique slanting letter manages to include abuse of a legal volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-off' looks like 'unique', but it means remove I (one), leaving TALIC from ITALIC. 'include' then wraps that round the word for slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the body of Jewish civil and religious law and its commentary.

clue.text: See 9
